target_roles.title: VP of Product Development
target_roles.rationale: As 3M's direct competitor in protective films with 8-9 year outdoor durability claims versus Tedlar's proven 12-20+ year performance, the VP of Product Development would be critically interested in understanding competitive differentiation gaps in their current overlaminate portfolio. They own product roadmap decisions and would care about Tedlar's superior UV resistance (no yellowing/fading/cracking), extreme temperature range (-70°F to 230°F vs typical vinyl limitations), and enhanced graffiti resistance that allows permanent markers and spray paint to clean off easily—features that could expose vulnerabilities in 3M's 8518/8519 Scotchcal series and anti-graffiti products (8588G, 8590M). With 3M actively launching new products like the Protection Wrap Film Color Series (2024), this role would be evaluating whether their fluoropolymer or alternative protective technologies can match or exceed Tedlar's 60+ years of proven field performance, especially as customers increasingly demand longer warranties and lower total cost of ownership. Their KPIs around product competitiveness, warranty claim rates, and premium market positioning make Tedlar's durability advantages directly relevant to their strategic planning and potential technology licensing or partnership considerations.

target_roles.title: Director of R&D
target_roles.rationale: With 3M operating as a materials science company with 60+ years in the graphics industry, the Director of R&D would be responsible for evaluating emerging protective film technologies and understanding competitive threats to their current product formulations. They would care deeply about Tedlar's polyvinyl fluoride (PVF) chemistry and how it achieves 12-20+ year outdoor durability compared to 3M's existing vinyl-based overlaminates. Given that 3M offers MCS warranties but only claims 8-9 years for their best overlaminates, R&D leadership would need to investigate whether Tedlar's proven field performance represents a technological advantage that could erode 3M's market position in premium architectural graphics, transit interiors, and long-term outdoor applications. Their technical evaluation would focus on Tedlar's mold/mildew resistance, chemical resistance to graffiti vandalism, and UV stability mechanisms that prevent color degradation—all critical to determining whether 3M needs to invest in next-generation protective film chemistry. This role's KPIs around innovation pipeline, competitive technical benchmarking, and materials performance data make them a key influencer in strategic technology decisions, including potential licensing, partnership, or defensive product development initiatives.

target_roles.title: Director of Strategic Sourcing
target_roles.rationale: While 3M manufactures protective films in-house, the Director of Strategic Sourcing would evaluate strategic supplier relationships for raw materials, specialty polymers, and potential co-branding opportunities that could enhance 3M's product portfolio. Given Tedlar's 60+ years of proven performance and superior durability claims (12-20+ years vs 8-9 years for 3M's best overlaminates), this role would assess whether incorporating DuPont Tedlar films into select 3M product lines could strengthen 3M's competitive position in ultra-premium segments where customers demand maximum longevity and lowest total cost of ownership. They would care about Tedlar's ability to reduce warranty claims, lower customer complaints about premature degradation, and enable 3M to offer extended warranty programs beyond their current MCS warranty terms. With 3M's recent product launches like the Protection Wrap Film Color Series and extensive installer training networks, Strategic Sourcing would evaluate whether a strategic partnership with DuPont could differentiate 3M's offerings in high-performance architectural panels (competing with DI-NOC), transit interiors requiring extreme durability, or specialized anti-graffiti applications where Tedlar's easy-clean properties exceed 3M's current 8588G/8590M capabilities. Their KPIs around supplier innovation, cost optimization, and strategic partnerships make them relevant for exploring collaborative opportunities rather than pure competitive positioning.
